summary:
What remains when humanity's greatest space mission is over? Beyond what humanity has discovered they leave behind extraordinary machines that once carried our curiosity beyond Earth, yet their stories are often forgotten.
	
	Welcome to Space Legacy, an interactive 3D educational platform developed to bring the stories of NASA’s forgotten space exploration hardware back to life. Throughout the platform the users can explore the Moon, Mars as well as the rest of the solar system. Users can also discover abandoned spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific equipment, and learn about the past missions. 

    Rather than simply present the historical face, Space Legacy uses interactive 3D environments, mission replay, visual storytelling, and educational information to help the user understand how those machinery and missions operated. Follow different stages of the space missions, from launching to landing in an engaging  storytelling from the narrator. 

   Space Legacy was designed specifically for the school-age students who are enthusiastic about space exploration. Transform complex scientific and historical information into accessible and immersive learning experiences. Who hopes Space Legacy will remind everyone that even though the mission ends, its discoveries and contribution continue to shape humanity's understanding of the universe.
details:
The Problem We Address

Space exploration is often remembered through its greatest discoveries, successful missions, and scientific achievements. However, the machines and equipment are often overlooked once their missions are complete. Their purposes, engineering designs, and contributions to science deserve to be remembered and understood.

Space Legacy will address this gap by transforming the stories of forgotten space equipment into an interactive experience where people can explore, learn, and appreciate the technology.

Vision and Mission 

Our Vision

To make the stories of space exploration accessible to everyone, inspiring people of all ages, especially young learners, to discover the wonders of space, appreciate human achievements, and imagine the possibilities of future exploration.

Our Mission

From stories of forgotten space equipment into engaging and easy-to-understand learning experiences through interactive storytelling, 3D visualizations, authentic NASA images, and real scientific data. We aim to make space history and science enjoyable, accessible, and meaningful for everyone.

Browse Mission

The Browse Missions section organizes space exploration into six destination-based categories making the user experience easier to discover the mission according to the region.  These categories include Earth Orbit, the Moon, Mars, the Sun, Mercury & Venus, Outer Planets & Beyond, and Asteroids & Comets. 

In the same Browse Mission tab, it has a Hardware Explorer which contains 64 space exploration objects, organized into seven hardware categories: Launch Vehicles, Spacecraft, Telescopes, Landers & Rovers, Scientific Instruments, Space Stations, and Return Capsules.

Throughout this section users can navigate different parts of the Solar System and select individual objects to explore the 3D model. This organization will help the users understand the mission’s contribution to our understanding of space and the technologies role involved in space exploration.

Mission Replay

The Mission Replay system allows users to experience selected historical missions through a sequence of interactive 3D scenes.

Each replay follows the actual stages relevant to that mission, rather than using one generic animation for every spacecraft. Depending on the mission, users can experience:

  • Launch and rocket liftoff.
  • Rocket stage separation and orbit insertion.
  • Interplanetary travel and spacecraft maneuvers.
  • Landing, orbital arrival, or equipment deployment.
  • Return to Earth and splashdown, where applicable.
  • Mission completion and final status.

A timeline, narration, captions, and playback controls help users follow the events and understand their significance.

Mission Simulator — Engineering Bay

The Engineering Bay allows users to experiment with the engineering decisions involved in building a space mission. It provides two modes:

Free Build (Sandbox Mode): Users can experiment with different components and create their own mission configurations. Combinations that have never flown are clearly identified as fictional.

This feature also introduces users to the importance of mission compatibility. Briefing explains potential limitations of the user's custom mission configuration  to the real engineering performance data. 

Astronaut Exploration &  AI Astronaut Assistance

After completing a simulated mission, users can continue into an interactive lunar or Martian environment.

Users can explore selected historical landing regions, move around as astronauts, operate vehicles, investigate scientific targets, and discover objects associated with previous missions.

The experience includes:

  • Walking, running, and jumping with movement adapted to the gravity of different worlds.
  • Driving the Lunar Roving Vehicle in selected Apollo landing environments.
  • Exploring Mars rover environments and interacting with scientific targets.
  • Recording discoveries, taking photographs, and collecting information about historical objects.

Another special function during the navigation of the region, the users will have AI Astronaut Assistance acts as their virtual guide throughout the experience. Rather than simply exploring the environment, users can learn the stories behind the objects they encounter through AI-powered storytelling.

My Collection 

This is the users collection from their past Mission Simulator. This will provide a revisit collected objects, read their information card, review the photographs and track their exploration progress. 

"While we explore new worlds, Space Legacy preserves the stories of those who came before." - KAMPU SPACE

NASA Data and Scientific Resources

Space Legacy uses NASA's scientific resources, mission records. By incorporating authentic NASA datasets and imagery, we aim to turn scientific information into accessible visual and interactive learning experiences.

NASA's resources also help us maintain historical accuracy and ensure that the stories presented throughout Space Legacy are supported by reliable evidence.

Tool, Technologies and Development

Space Legacy was developed as a browser-based application using the following technologies:

The project currently uses vanilla JavaScript ES modules and a Three.js CDN import map, without requiring a separate build process. 

Intended Impact

Our goal is to make the history and achievements of space exploration more accessible, engaging, and meaningful to everyone. We hope Space Legacy will encourage students to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), while raising awareness about the abandoned technology and equipment in outer space.
